test_input: Start the game by running the program. Use the arrow keys to change direction while the snake automatically moves. Example play sequence: hold RIGHT for a few seconds to move right, then press UP, LEFT, DOWN as needed to navigate. Eat food squares to increase score. When GAME OVER appears, press R to restart and confirm snake resets to center and score resets to 0. Press ESC at any time to quit.
expected_win_output: No win condition in this game. Play continues until the snake collides with a wall or itself. (No WIN message is produced by the program.)
expected_lose_output:
When the game ends the program prints the line:
GAME OVER
Additionally, every time the score increases the program prints lines like:
[EVENT] SCORE:1
[EVENT] SCORE:2
... 
On restart (R) if the score changes to 0 the program prints the updated score (e.g. "[EVENT] SCORE:0"). The final score is also shown on the GAME OVER overlay in the window.
notes:
Implementation notes and known limitations:
- Rendering: The grid is 20x20, cell size 30 pixels, header area 80 px. Resolution is 600x680 and FPS fixed at 10 as required.
- Graphics: Plain colored rectangles only (procedural). No sounds.
- Controls: Arrow keys to move, R to restart (resets snake, food and score), Esc to quit.
- Score print: Every time score changes the new score is printed to stdout as required.
- Reset: R fully restores initial snake (3 segments centered), score 0, and spawns new food excluding the snake.
- Files implementing features: game/snake_game.py (main loop, rendering, UI, input, score, reset, prints), game/snake.py (snake positions, movement, growth, self-collision guard), game/food.py (food spawn logic). 
- Limitations: No pause feature. No high-score persistence. Food spawn uses Python's random and may place food in unpredictable but valid positions. The game uses pygame.font.Font(None, size) so it doesn't rely on system fonts.
- Automated tests: Boot/syntax checks passed in the sandbox; interactive behavior must be validated manually by running the program and using keyboard inputs.
